q-36485.name: Question 1
q-36485.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $C$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $C$ are given below. What is $[x]_{B}?$ 

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$
q-36485.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ from $C$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 3 & -4\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-2)\cdot (-4)-3\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}-4 & -3 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

The change-of-coordinates matrix from B to C and the coordinates of the vector x relative to the basis C are given below. What is [x]B?

PB→C=[−233−4],[x]C=[3−2]

a
[5−6]
b
[65]
c
[−25]
d
[6−4]
e
[−56]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

[x]B=PC→B[x]C.

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix PC→B from C to B. To do that, we compute the inverse of PB→C:

PC→B=PB→C−1=[−233−4]−1=1(−2)⋅(−4)−3⋅3[−4−3−3−2]=[4332]

Now, we compute [x]B:

[x]B=PC→B[x]C=[4332][3−2]=[65]

q-113573.name: Question 2
q-113573.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ to $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$ is given below. Find $[x]_{B}$ given that $x=2{c}_{1}-4{c}_{2}.$

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 5 & -8\end{aligned}]
$$
q-113573.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ from $C$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 5 & -8\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\cdot (-8)-(-3)\cdot 5}[\begin{aligned}-8 & 3 \\ -5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -3 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that since $x=2{c}_{1}-4{c}_{2},$ we obtain

$$
[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -3 \\ 5 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}28 \\ 18\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-113603.name: Question 3
q-113603.problem:
$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\},\,[x]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$

The basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the standard basis $S$ are given above. Find $[x]_{B}.$
q-113603.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S}.
$$

First, recall that the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is the matrix whose columns are the vectors of $B$ relative to the standard basis $S.$ As a result, we have

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}5 & 6 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{S\to B}$ from $S$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to S}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S\to B} & ={P}_{B\to S}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}5 & 6 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5\cdot 4-6\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 \\ -3 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}8 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-113606.name: Question 4
q-113606.problem:
$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 6\end{aligned}]\},\,[x]_{S}=[\begin{aligned}18 \\ -9\end{aligned}]
$$

The basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the standard basis $S$ are given above. Find $[x]_{B}.$
q-113606.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S}.
$$

First, recall that the change-of-coordinates matrix from $B$ to $S$ is the matrix whose columns are the vectors of $B$ relative to the standard basis $S.$ As a result, we have

$$
{P}_{B\to S}=[\begin{aligned}5 & -7 \\ -3 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{S\to B}$ from $S$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to S}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S\to B} & ={P}_{B\to S}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}5 & -7 \\ -3 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5\cdot 6-(-7)\cdot (-3)}[\begin{aligned}6 & 7 \\ 3 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} & \frac{7}{9} \\ \frac{1}{3} & \frac{5}{9}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} & \frac{7}{9} \\ \frac{1}{3} & \frac{5}{9}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}18 \\ -9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-113615.name: Question 5
q-113615.problem:
$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\},\,C=\{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\},\,[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The bases $B$ and $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $C$ are given above. Find $[x]_{B}.$
q-113615.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ and $C$ as $\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ and $\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$, respectively.

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $C$ to $B$ is a matrix whose columns are the vectors of $C$ relative to the basis $B.$

Hence, we need to find the coordinates of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ relative to the basis $B.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we simply reduce the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 4 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ is

$$
{P}_{C\to B}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2} & -4 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2} & -4 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

B={[22],[34]},C={[23],[14]},[x]C=[−21]

The bases B and C of R2 and the coordinates of the vector x relative to the basis C are given above. Find [x]B.

a
[11−4]
b
[4−5]
c
[−13]
d
[136]
e
[−31]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's denote the vectors of B and C as {b1,b2} and {c1,c2}, respectively.

The change-of-coordinates matrix from C to B is a matrix whose columns are the vectors of C relative to the basis B.

Hence, we need to find the coordinates of c1 and c2 relative to the basis B. We can do this simultaneously by considering the matrix M=[||||b1b2c1c2||||].

Now, we simply reduce the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

M=[23212434]R2:=R2+(−1)R1∼[23210113]R1:=R1+(−3)R2∼[20−1−80113]R1:=12R1∼[10−12−40113]

Therefore, the change-of-coordinates matrix PC→B is

PC→B=[−12−413].

Finally, we compute [x]B:

[x]B=PC→B[x]C=[−12−413][−21]=[−31]
